segments.text: "Welcome to Robot Roundup, your daily dose of robotics news.
I'm your host, and we're kicking off another day in the world of artificial intelligence and machine learning on August 11th, 2026.
Today, we'll dive into the latest advancements in robotics, from human-like touch sensing to autonomous trucking, with PlusAI pushing its safety readiness over 90 percent."
From Humanoids Daily, "Dyna-2 Proves Scaling Laws for Robotics: 1 Million Hours of Human Video Unlocks Zero-Shot Dexterity".
Dyna-2 has demonstrated a human-to-robot transfer scaling law, proving that scaling human video predictably improves zero-shot performance on unseen robot hardware.
The model achieved an 87% pass rate in real-world zero-shot deployments, outperforming its predecessor, Dyna-1, and marking a significant milestone in robotics research.

Dyna-2 was pre-trained on over one million hours of human video data using the "video co-training" method, where the model is trained in parallel with humans performing actions to be replicated by robots.
This approach enables the model to learn from human interactions and adapt to new robot hardware with unprecedented flexibility.
The novel architecture also introduced a one-step video generation distillation pipeline, significantly reducing inference latency.
The achievement showcases Dyna-2's capabilities as a pioneering solution for robotics and highlights its potential to unlock zero-shot dexterity in robots.
From Robotics & Automation News, "PlusAI reaches ‘93.4 percent safety readiness’ ahead of autonomous truck launch."
PlusAI has achieved a significant milestone in its development process, marking 93.4 percent Safety Case Readiness ahead of its planned commercial launch of factory-built driverless trucks in 2027.

The company has reported substantial advancements, including an increase to 99.8 percent Autonomous Miles Percentage and a rise to 85.2 percent Remote Assistance Free Trips during the first half of 2026.
This progress enables PlusAI to expect reaching 100 percent Safety Case Readiness by 2027 and targets over 90 percent of trips without remote assistance at commercial launch.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Electronic skin gives robots and prosthetics ‘human-like touch sensing’.

Researchers at Hanyang University ERICA have developed a vertically integrated dual-gated tribotronic transistor architecture that offers tuneable sensitivity, reliable contact and proximity detection, and minimal pixel footprint for high-density array integration.
This technology can pave the way for electronic skin systems that allow robots and prosthetics to reliably perceive human touch.

The device exhibits stable response and recovery times of 127 and 212 milliseconds during each contact-separation cycle, demonstrating its suitability for applications in healthcare robots, health monitoring, and autonomous systems.
By harnessing this innovation, researchers aim to create more advanced robotic capabilities with improved sensing and interaction, further expanding the possibilities of human-robot collaboration.
From Robohub, "A ‘5-in-1’ seed-sized surgical robot"
reports on scientists at Nanyang Technological University in Singapore who have developed a revolutionary new device.

The researchers created a tiny surgical robot that can perform five distinct functions wirelessly on soft and uneven surfaces, including cutting biological tissues, releasing drugs, gripping tissue samples, and generating heat remotely.
The robot, measuring just 4.4 mm in length, utilizes magnetic coils and soft magnetic materials to control its movements and switch between different functions within a mere second.
To test the device's capabilities, the researchers employed biological tissues, revealing minimal damage or adverse effects during the performance of the specified functions.
This breakthrough demonstrates the immense potential for miniaturized robots in surgical procedures.

This innovation could significantly advance the field of robotics and artificial intelligence, paving the way for more efficient and precise medical treatments with miniature devices that can navigate complex surfaces with unprecedented precision.
From IEEE Spectrum - Robotics, "Robot Recycler Salvages Parts from Broken Machines."
Researchers at the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology have designed a system that enables predictive disassembly of broken robots, resulting in salvaged valuable parts without causing damage.
The system employs a predictive algorithm and robotic manipulators to break down the robot, with updates made based on observations and real-time data analysis.
This innovative approach aims to create a circular economy where old devices are repurposed to make new ones, reducing electronic waste.

The system's methodology involves collecting data from the broken robot and feeding it into the predictive algorithm, which then determines the most efficient disassembly sequence to minimize part loss and damage.
The robotic manipulators execute the plan, carefully disassembling the robot while preserving critical components.
This process is repeated in real-time, allowing for continuous monitoring of the system's performance.
This breakthrough technology has significant implications for the AI and tech industry, as it paves the way for the development of more efficient and sustainable device recycling practices.

As this field continues to evolve, expect to see further innovations in robotic disassembly and repair methods, ultimately driving towards a more circular and environmentally conscious approach to electronic waste management.
From Robotics & Automation News, "Interview with Maximo’s Nick Hegeman: 180,000 robotic installations of solar panels and counting."
This story reports on the rapid adoption of Maximo's AI-powered robotic system in the construction industry, particularly for installing solar panels.
Maximo has now installed over 180,000 solar panels, representing more than 100 MW of generating capacity.
The robots using this technology have exceeded 500 installations per day, with crews equipped with Maximo achieving up to 24 modules per person per shift hour.

According to Nick Hegeman, chief commercial officer for Maximo, customer adoption can be attributed to the ease of integration and reliable performance of their system, which has transformed robotics from an unproven technology into a practical construction tool.
This milestone marks significant progress in the adoption of AI-powered robotic systems in the construction industry, showcasing their potential for increased efficiency and productivity.
"Alright, we're shutting down the factory for today - but the robots won't stop!
Thanks for joining us on this day's dose of robotic bliss.
Until next time, keep your circuits charged and your dexterity sharp - see you in the next cycle!"
